stops.note: literally 'to rise up', from sub- 'up from below' and regere 'to guide'
the feminine past participle was nominalized for troops rushing out of a besieged position
stops.meaning: a going out; an attack by the besieged on besiegers

stops.note: kept its siege-warfare sense, then in the First World War was extended to a single flight by a military aircraft
stops.meaning: a mission flown by one military aircraft

current_meaning: an attacking or reconnaissance flight by a single military aircraft
